panels.rationale: Single-panel color Doppler ultrasound of the penis performed in the article's newborn with priapism; the caption states 'Normal arterial flow on Colour Doppler Ultrasonography (CDU) of the penis in our newborn with priapism' and the in-text mention notes that after this examination 'non-ischemic priapism' was confirmed, with detumescence after conservative treatment. Patent/normal cavernosal arterial flow on Doppler is the defining hemodynamic feature of non-ischemic (high-flow) priapism, so the panel is attributed to priapism and mapped to the closest allowed finding key (high-flow cavernosal arterial flow on Doppler ultrasound); the wording 'normal' rather than 'increased' flow is recorded in proposed_findings. Real patient image (neonate), ultrasound modality, no skin visible so skin tone is null; no ethnicity stated. Figure is a single non-compound image with on-screen measurement calipers/scale annotations. Confidence is moderate because the caption describes normal rather than frankly increased arterial flow and the diagnosis rests on the article's statement of non-ischemic priapism. [raw subtype: non-ischemic (high-flow) priapism]
